title: Chart.js Practice
description: Practise the twelve ideas in this Chart.js course. Choose an answer, then read why it fits the example.

exercises.question: What does each bar height represent?
options: The number of letters in the label
exercises.explanation: A bar chart compares amounts between categories. Chart.js pairs labels with the values in a dataset.

exercises.question: What does the dataset label explain?
exercises.explanation: A dataset label explains what a set of values measures. It can appear in the legend and tooltips.

exercises.question: What makes days suitable for this line chart?
exercises.explanation: A line chart can show how a value changes across an ordered sequence, such as days.

exercises.question: Which category is half of the total?
exercises.explanation: A doughnut chart shows shares of a total. It works best with a small number of clearly labelled categories.

exercises.question: What does one scatter point contain?
options: An x and a y measurement
exercises.explanation: A scatter chart places each item using an x value and a y value. It can show how two measurements relate.

exercises.question: Why start this bar axis at zero?
options: To force every bar to have the same height
To make bar lengths compare amounts honestly
exercises.explanation: A bar's length should make comparisons clear. Starting its numeric axis at zero usually avoids exaggerating small differences.

exercises.question: Why label both datasets?
options: To explain which bars represent which measure
exercises.explanation: Two datasets can share the same categories. Each needs a clear label and a distinguishable style.

exercises.question: What asks Chart.js to redraw changed data?
exercises.explanation: A chart instance can receive changed data. Calling update redraws it from the new values.

exercises.question: Which element supplies the chart layout size here?
exercises.explanation: A responsive chart uses its parent container to decide its display size. The parent needs a clear size when the aspect ratio is not maintained.

exercises.question: Which option disables chart animation?
exercises.explanation: Chart animation can be disabled when it is not useful. This can make repeated updates easier to follow and reduce motion.

exercises.question: Why provide text outside canvas?
options: To make the information usable without the drawing
exercises.explanation: Canvas drawings do not contain normal readable HTML rows. Give the chart a name and provide its values as text or a table.

exercises.question: Which method releases the Chart.js instance?
exercises.explanation: A chart can keep event listeners and drawing resources. Destroy the instance when its canvas or page part is removed.
